summary: The study describes a thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) process for producing MoS2 thin films using bis(tert-butylimido)-bis(dimethylamido)molybdenum and 1-propanethiol. The process exhibits self-limiting behavior with respect to both precursors at 350 °C, resulting in a growth per cycle of approximately 0.1 nm/cycle. As-deposited films are amorphous and contain nitrogen and carbon impurities, which are removed upon high-temperature annealing, leading to few-layer crystalline 2H-MoS2 films.
evidence: The authors observe a self-limiting reaction behavior with respect to both the Mo and S precursors at a substrate temperature of 350 °C. Film thickness scales linearly with precursor cycling, with growth per cycle values of ≈0.1 nm/cycle. Upon high-temperature annealing, a large portion of the impurities are removed, and the authors obtain few-layer crystalline 2H-MoS2 films.
